jobs.occupation: Management Consultant / Manager – Financial Services
jobs.description:
Join Accenture Financial Services

Do you want to help leading Nordic banks, insurers and capital markets firms shape their future, navigate complex business challenges, and translate strategic ambitions into tangible business results?

Join our Financial Services team in Copenhagen, where we combine deep industry knowledge, business strategy, functional expertise and transformation capabilities. You will help leading financial institutions address their most pressing business challenges, shape strategic priorities and translate ambitions into measurable results.

You will work with colleagues acress Banking, Insurance and Capital Markets and collaborate with specialists from across Accenture on projects spanning business strategy, commercial development, customer experience, operating model design and large-scale transformation, with data, AI and technology as key enablers.

The role offers the opportunity to work closely with leading financial institutions on their key strategic priorities, build on the experience you already bring, deepen your industry knowledge and take increasing ownership of client engagements and strategic initiatives as you progress.

What you will do

As a Management Consultant or Manager in our Financial Services team, you will join multidisciplinary teams that bring together deep industry knowledge, business strategy, functional expertise and transformation capabilities. You will help leading financial institutions address key business challenges, shape strategic priorities and translate ambitions into measurable results.

Depending on your experience and role, you may:

• Support or lead workstreams within business strategy, growth, operating model and large-scale transformation engagements.

• Analyze market dynamics, competitive landscapes, customer needs and business performance to identify opportunities and develop strategic recommendations.

• Help clients define strategic priorities, develop business cases and translate business ambitions into actionable transformation roadmaps.

• Design and implement future business and operating models, customer propositions, processes and ways of working.

• Explore how digital innovation, data, AI and emerging technologies can enable new business opportunities, improve customer experiences and drive operational efficiency.

• Develop and present strategic insights, business cases and recommendations to senior client stakeholders.

• Collaborate with client leadership and cross-functional teams to solve complex business challenges and drive transformation.

• Contribute to business development, client proposals, thought leadership and the continued growth of our Financial Services practice.

You will work directly with clients, with a level of ownership that reflects your experience – from driving analyses, developing recommendations and engaging with stakeholders to leading workstreams, advising client leadership and guiding junior team members.

Who we are

We are Accenture’s Financial Services Industry & Enterprise team in Copenhagen, bringing together colleagues with backgrounds in consulting, financial services, business and technology. We work across Banking, Insurance and Capital Markets, supporting financial institutions through business and technology transformation.

We are a local team within a broader Nordic and global Financial Services practice. In our project work, we combine local market and industry knowledge with specialist capabilities from across Accenture. Day to day, you will work with colleagues from different parts of the organization while remaining closely connected to our Copenhagen team.

What we are looking for

We are looking for people who have already relevant experience and want to continue building on it. You are not expected to know every part of financial services from day one, but you should have a solid professional foundation, a genuine interest in the industry and the motivation to develop further.

We imagine that you:

• Hold a relevant Master’s degree in business, economics, finance, technology, engineering or a related field.

• Have 2 - 5 years of relevant professional experience, for example from consulting, a financial institution, fintech or a comparable business or technology transformation role.

• Have strong analytical and problem-solving skills and enjoy working with complex topics.

• Can structure complex information and turn it into clear conclusions and recommendations.

• Are interested in financial services and the role of technology, data and AI in shaping the industry.

• Direct experience in banking, insurance, capital markets or fintech is an advantage, particularly when combined with consulting or transformation experience.

• Communicate clearly and feel comfortable engaging with different stakeholders.

• Enjoy working collaboratively while taking ownership of your responsibilities.

• Are fluent in English, proficiency in Danish or another Nordic language is an advantage.

• Resident in Denmark

What’s in it for you

Development: Build your consulting skills and Financial Services expertise through project work, formal training, and regular feedback.

Responsibility: Take ownership in line with your experience, with opportunities to lead deliverables, workstreams and client interactions.

Broad experience, room to specialize: Work across different clients and topics while gradually developing your own area of expertise.

A strong network: Work with colleagues and specialists across Copenhagen, the Nordics, Netherlands, and Accenture’s global organization.

Career support: Develop your career with guidance from experienced colleagues and a dedicated People Lead.

A social Copenhagen team: Be based in our Carlsberg Byen office, where we regularly come together for team events and informal gatherings alongside project work.

An inclusive workplace: Work in an environment where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued.

Get in touch

If you have questions about the role or our Financial Services team, feel free to contact Pedro Monteiro, Danish Financial Services Lead, at pedro.c.monteiro@accenture.com or Sebastian Lundgaard, Danish Banking & Capital Markets Lead, at sebastian.lundgaard@accenture.com or Kasper Kai, Danish Insurance Lead, at kasper.kai@accenture.com.

Apply now

Apply online and remember to attach your CV, cover letter and university grades. We look forward to receiving your application.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in applied microbial dynamics for tropical farm fermentations - BRIGHT
jobs.description:
Are you interested in microbial ecology and food fermentation, and at the same time eager to work towards more sustainable food systems? Then join us as our new PhD Student in tropical farm fermentations

The overwhelming majority of coffee and cocoa are produced in the tropics, and represent vast economic drivers globally as these products continue to transform from commodities to luxury goods. Alongside other factors, the quality of these goods is largely influenced by post-harvest processing, which modulates microbial activity, in turn leading to differences in sensory impact. Complex microbial dynamics affect fermentation outcomes and sensory attributes, and understanding these dynamics and how relevant microbial consortia can be mobilised to modulate these outcomes pose challenging questions that can lead to multiple applications, including ones with health implications. This project aims to unravel some of the underlying microbial dynamics of tropical fermentations such as coffee, cocoa, or other traditional tropical fermentation, utilizing a combination of metagenomics, strain characterization, and solid-state fermentation.

This position is part of a wider cross-institutional research programme on “Microbial fermentation innovations for a resilient food system, optimised human health and environmental sustainability”. You will be working at the interface of biotechnology, genetics, and fermentation in a cutting-edge interdisciplinary and multi-cultural research environment, and will have the opportunity to go on research stay (one-year minimum, preferably two) with our partner institution the Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE) department at the Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI) under the Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR) in Singapore.

The job
As our PhD student in tropical farm fermentations, you will:

• Analyse metagenomic profiles of artisanal tropical fermentations
• Characterise extant yeast and bacteria for relevant traits for fermentative capability and other functional capacities
• Perform solid state fermentations in controlled settings to achieve targeted outcomes
• Evaluate fermentations via microbiology, molecular biology, and analytic chemistry
• Validate effects of post-fermentation processing on physicochemical qualities and aroma profiles
• Explore potential environmental and socio-economic ramifications of luxury commodities from tropical farm fermentations
What we’re looking for
You will have a two-year Master’s degree (120 ECTS points) in molecular biology, genetics, biotechnology, microbiology, or closely related disciplines, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year Master's degree.

You will have excellent organizational and project management skills and enjoy developing new methods.

You will be fluent in spoken and written English and have literacy in common IT systems

The ideal candidate will also:

• have experience with molecular biology techniques and, ideally, some foundational understanding in metagenomics, microbial ecology, microbiology, analytical chemistry and/or sensory science
• have a genuine interest in food systems and sustainability
• be able to work with others and independently, and adaptable to working in multi-cultural environments
• be comfortable in an interdisciplinary environment, and a willingness to bridge microbial biotechnology with food and sensory science
• be patient, charitable, curious and playful—key qualities for interdisciplinary work
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by co-supervisors, Dr. Tiffany Mak and Dr. Eric Peterson, and primary supervisor, Prof. Morten Sommer.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The period of employment is 3 years, full time. 

Start date is 01-04-2027 or according to mutual agreement. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
For additional information about the position, please contact Researcher Tiffany Mak at tifmak@dtu.dk, or Senor Scientist Eric Peterson at Eric_Peterson@a-star.edu.sg. 

You can read more about BRIGHT below, and at www.bright.dtu.dk 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae

Candidates will be invited to the first round of interviews between 7-11 January 2027.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Microbial Foods Group
The Microbial Foods Group is focused on exploring fundamental microbial processes within our food system from a planetary health perspective. We are committed to addressing pressing global food systems and sustainability challenges through integrated and multi-scalar approaches. A key goal is to understand and develop microbially-driven processes that can be effectively implemented to substantially reduce the environmental impact of our current food production system.

BRIGHT – The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition
The Novo Nordisk Foundation Biotechnology Research Institute for the Green Transition (BRIGHT) is a major initiative based at DTU that aims to accelerate the development of biosolutions and strengthen the bio-based economy. BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. BRIGHT focuses on three main areas: Sustainable materials (Developing bio-based alternatives to fossil-derived materials), Microbial foods (Innovating food production through microbial technologies), and Microorganisms for net-zero agriculture (Creating solutions to reduce greenhouse gas emissions in agriculture). The goal is to develop and scale innovative biosolutions within these areas, ultimately creating sustainable and competitive alternatives to fossil-based products and processes that can make significant contributions to reducing global greenhouse gas emissions.

Biotransformation & Engineering (BTE)
The Biotransformation & Engineering division brings together the complementary expertise of Biotransformation and Strain Engineering to form a dynamic and synergistic hub for sustainable innovation. By seamlessly integrating advanced biotransformation technologies with precision strain engineering, we drive the creation of high-value compounds, including nutraceuticals, flavors, personal care ingredients, and functional bioactives. As a unified force of innovation and sustainability, the division combines strengths in biocatalysis, fermentation, strain engineering, and synthetic biology to pioneer science-driven solutions that are shaping the future of food and consumer care industries.

Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation (SIFBI)
The A*STAR Singapore Institute of Food and Biotechnology Innovation brings together biotechnology, food and sensory science, nutrition and digestive health to create sustainable ingredients and consumer-driven health solutions for Asia. From discovery and biomanufacturing to product design and human validation, we help partners translate science into meaningful outcomes for people, industry and Singapore.

Agency for Science, Research and Technology (A*STAR)
The Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) is Singapore's lead public sector R&D agency. Through open innovation, we collaborate with our partners in both the public and private sectors to benefit the economy and society. As a Science and Technology Organisation, A*STAR bridges the gap between academia and industry. Our research creates economic growth and jobs for Singapore, and enhances lives by improving societal outcomes in healthcare, urban living, and sustainability. A*STAR plays a key role in nurturing scientific talent and leaders for the wider research community and industry. A*STAR's R&D activities span biomedical sciences to physical sciences and engineering, with research entities primarily located in Biopolis and Fusionopolis.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Existing microbial food productions have largely focused on liquid state fermentation as the main production strategy under industrial settings. This approach however limits the media composition, excluding the potential use of substrates with lower solubility, as well as substrates mixtures that are heterogeneous by nature. Additionally, there are notable environmental impacts of large-scale liquid state fermenters, especially in terms of freshwater use, both during the fermentation process, as well as downstream purification steps. Furthermore, many existing fermentation approaches rely on pure isolates of microbial starter cultures, which limits the potential functional benefits when compared to mixed microbial communities, both in terms of the functional qualities (including taste, texture and nutrition) of the final product, as well as the safety and robustness of the fermentation process.

This project therefore seeks to address some of these limitations by exploring the potential of using microbial consortia for solid-state fermentation (SSF) in microbial foods production. A key focus will be on identifying and characterising promising fungal-bacterial interactions in mixed microbial consortia, and evaluating their respective influences on different fermentation outcomes and functional qualities, with a focus on the nutritional composition and other potential human health modulating factors of the final microbial food.

jobs.occupation: Research Data Management & Digital Infrastructure Officer
jobs.description:
Can you combine technical understanding, stakeholder management, and practical execution to advance research data and IT initiatives across a complex organization?

  The Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND) at the University of Copenhagen (UCPH) is one of Europe's leading health faculties and home to the recently established Center for Core Facilities (CCF), which brings together world-class research infrastructures to support excellence in research, innovation, and education. 

  To further strengthen CCF's digital capabilities, we are seeking a proactive and solutions-oriented Research Data Management & Digital Infrastructure Officer to co-design and implement a data management and digital infrastructure framework across the Center. Working closely with the University of Copenhagen IT Department (UCPH-IT) and data experts from CCF's core facilities, the successful candidate will help develop sustainable solutions that support cutting-edge research and technology platforms.

  About the Role - The role combines research data management, stakeholder coordination, and IT technical expertise to ensure that users generating data at CCF's research infrastructures have access to data services to optimally collect, annotate, store and FAIR share AI-ready quality data.

  The successful candidate will become part of a highly international and interdisciplinary center, working closely with technology and data experts at CCF, UCPH-IT, and national and international key stakeholders to create a multi-technology data infrastructure and management ecosystem towards quality AI-ready data. 

  As leading force of the CCF Data Infrastructure Working Group, the successful candidate will have the following Key Responsibilities:

   	
• Drive the design and implementation of a CCF research data infrastructure, with particular focus on efficient and optimal data processing, analysis, storage and file systems. 	
• Lead and support research data management activities, including FAIRification of data practices and data lifecycle management. 	
• Maintain oversight of CCF data assets, including ownership, retention, storage, and deletion processes. 	
• Serve as the primary interface between CCF Core Facilities and external stakeholders (incl. UCPH-IT, DeiC, ELIXIR, EOSC and others), ensuring effective operation of CCF data infrastructure. 	
• Advise on data security, data governance, and compliance with institutional policies and relevant regulations. 	
• Identify, implement, and improve tools and workflows that support, improve and optimize CCF research data management. 	
• Track ongoing initiatives, maintain institutional knowledge, and help drive projects to completion.   We are looking for a person that has:

   	
• Experience with research data management and FAIR data principles. 	
• Strong understanding of IT infrastructure, particularly computing and storage systems and file management. 	
• Familiarity with GDPR, institutional data policies, and large-scale IT projects is an advantage. 	
• Experience coordinating complex projects involving multiple stakeholders. 	
• Ability to translate researchers' needs into technical requirements and vice versa. 	
• Knowledge of information security and data governance. 	
• Experience working with research environments is highly desirable. 	
• Fluent English is a must, and Danish is an asset.   We are looking for a candidate who is:

   	
• Proactive, persistent, and able to drive initiatives forward. 	
• Comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders and advocating for researchers' needs. 	
• Willing to challenge the status quo and propose new solutions. 	
• Equally capable of strategic thinking and hands-on implementation. 	
• An effective communicator who can build bridges between researchers and IT professionals. 	
• Organized, collaborative, and focused on achieving practical outcomes.   Terms of salary and employment
 The successful candidate will join the CCF Administration and Development team, To start with, the employment is a full-time one-year term position, as it is linked to a pilot grant. However, our vision is to work with the successful candidate to create a financial model to sustain data services beyond the grant period. 

  Employment will be as a special consultant in accordance with the applicable collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and academics in the state (the AC collective agreement). It is possible to negotiate supplements according to qualifications. The employer will pay an additional 18,07 % to your pension fund.

 Send your application with your CV and relevant documentation via the Job Portal (click on "APPLY FOR THE POSITION" at the bottom of the advertisement) so that it is received by us no later than 22 December 2026.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Abrasive Flow Polishing of Metallic, Ceramic, and Multi-Material Impellers - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
The Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering of the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) has an open PhD position on the topic of “Abrasive flow polishing of metallic, ceramic, and multi-material impellers”.

The position is in the context of the project Turbo Impact - TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology, a new Marie Skłodowska Curie (MSCA) Doctoral Network Programme funded by the European Commission, that brings together 6 universities and 12 industry partners from 9 countries. Find more information at https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350.

Turbo Impact trains a new generation of creative and innovative manufacturing and materials researchers, with strong analytical, computational, and experimental skills and a deep understanding of all aspects of producing metallic, ceramic and multi-material small scale turbomachinery components and systems. In the framework of the doctoral network, the PhD student will work closely with a cohort of 14 PhD students working on different but related topics within the domain of turbomachinery components design and manufacturing.

General and project specific eligibility requirements
All applicants must fulfil the following general eligibility criteria, or otherwise will be rejected:

• must have completed a Master's degree or equivalent at the time of start.
• must not have a doctoral degree at the date of their recruitment;
• must comply with the mobility rules, where they must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting organization for more than 12 months, at any point during the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date (short stays such as holidays or compulsory military service are not taken into account);
Essential language requirements
The working language of Turbo Impact is English.

Responsibilities and qualifications
The PhD position is hosted by DTU Construct's Section for Manufacturing Engineering. The research focuses on the development, modelling and experimental validation of abrasive flow polishing process for precision metallic, ceramic and multi-material components used in high-performance turbomachinery applications. 

The project aims to develop processes, fixtures, tools and models enabling time- and space-controlled material removal applied to AM-produced multi-material components to support ultra-fine surface finish and structural integrity of surface and subsurface, for improved component performance, durability and reliability. 

Key research activities include:

• Development of micro/nano scale material removal modelling for abrasive flow polishing of small-scale shrouded impellers.
• Development of innovative small/micro flow polishing setup including sensing and control.
• Application of developed process solutions to realization of small-scale shrouded impellers for validation of improvements. 
The project will utilize a combination of existing and newly developed equipment to generate data, produce test parts and implement closed loop control. Industrial validation will be conducted in collaboration with partner companies.

The position involves both theoretical and experimental work, with responsibilities spanning project execution and academic dissemination. The candidate will be expected to:

• Position the scientific work within the context of current literature.
• Collaborate with academic and industrial partners through workshops, case studies, and co-development activities.
• Publish findings in peer-reviewed journals and present results at international conferences.
• Contribute to teaching, supervision, and student activities within the Section for Manufacturing Engineering.
We are looking for candidates with:

• An excellent academic background in production engineering, mechanical engineering, materials engineering or related fields.
• Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes and systems applied to metallic and ceramic materials and related characterization techniques. 
• Experience with manufacturing metrology and programming tools such as MATLAB or Python.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data for mapping submerged landscapes and archaeological potential
jobs.description:
The Department of Geoscience, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data, with the aim of identifying submerged landscapes and locations of archaeological potential. We are searching for a motivated and engaged researcher with experience in inversion to be part of our research team studying late Quaternary and Holocene processes and landscape evolution.

The postdoctoral position is a fixed-term full-time position for 1 year.

The postdoctoral work will be part of the international ERC Synergy Grant project SUBNORDICA, where scientists in the fields of geology, geophysics, and archaeology work together to develop methodologies for recreating submerged landscapes and human settlement in NW Europe, and for finding submerged Stone Age settlements in deeper water settings such as the North Sea. SUBNORDICA also uses machine-learning routines to identify, from existing and new data, targets of archaeological potential for more detailed investigation. The research team at the department is leading a work package focused on the eastern North Sea region. Other members in the team work on geophysical imaging methods, sea level modelling, and palaeolandscape mapping to generate palaeotopography and palaeocoastlines using both legacy and newly acquired data.

Job description
The postdoctoral position is focused on probabilistic inversion of seismic data to estimate subsurface properties that can be linked directly to the location of submerged settlements – a key example being the presence of peat, which marks former dry land.

Specific tasks will be to:

• Develop probabilistic inversion workflows for high-resolution subbottom profiles and multichannel seismic data from the North Sea, constrained by sediment core observations
• Map peat and other landscape types relevant for archaeology, and use the results together with machine-learning routines to identify targets of archaeological potential
• Provide input and constraints for predictive modelling workflows carried out at partner institutions
The postdoctoral researcher will be working closely together with post docs and senior staff in the research team at the department, as well as with the international partners in the SUBNORDICA project. Close collaboration is expected particularly with partners focused on predictive modelling for archaeology. The position provides opportunities for offshore field work and participation in joint research expeditions in the North Sea and Baltic Sea. It is also expected that the postdoc will take an active part in various research team activities and contribute to supervision and teaching of (under-) graduate students in the team.

Facilities
Laboratory facilities at the Department of Geoscience will be available for the position. This includes the acquisition, processing and interpretation facilities at SeisLab Aarhus for both multi- and single channel marine seismic and acoustic data, and an advanced sediment core laboratory.

Qualifications
The qualified applicant will have a PhD degree in geoscience, geophysics or related fields. Candidates should preferably have a background within probabilistic inversion and uncertainty quantification and/or machine learning. Experience with seismic data, including reflection seismic and hydroacoustic data, is beneficial, as is experience with linking seismic data to physical or lithological properties. Experience with the shallow subsurface of the North Sea or other similar settings, including sediment cores and marine geoarchaeology, is further beneficial but not required.

The candidate is expected to have well-documented research experience with academic publications and presentations at conferences and meetings. The applicant should also have effective organizational skills, with previous project management being beneficial. The candidate should be able to work collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team of geophysicists, geologists and archaeologists. Oral and written English skills are required.

Application

• Cover Letter, including motivation for applying and information on how the candidate’s qualifications and experience will aid the project

• PhD certificate or a statement regarding the expected date of completing of PhD studies

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Statistical learning as a tool to understand host-microbiome-flavour interactions in plant growth
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a two-year position at the University of Copenhagen, as part of the ongoing Novo Nordisk Foundation funded project ‘Tomatoponics’. The goal of the project is to apply statistical and machine learning tools to multi-omics data including plant genotypes, root microbiomes and fruit shotgun metabolomes to better understand how the host and microbiome affect the fruit flavour. We aim to go beyond genotype-phenotype associations to reveal causal pathways, that will be tested in future trials.

  The candidate will be principally advised by Assoc. Prof. Shyam Gopalakrishnan, who leads the FindingPheno project based at the Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics (https://ceh.ku.dk), with additional guidance from Prof Tom Gilbert, Director of the Center. The Gopalakrishnan research group focuses on using population and statistical genetics to understand genotype-phenotype associations with a special focus on the role of microbiomes in evolutionary processes.

  Information on the department can be found at https://globe.ku.dk.

  Your job

  You will analyse a pre-generated dataset consisting of root metagenomes, resequenced plant genomes, untargeted fruit metabolomes plus other phenotypic data from a dataset of 10 cultivars exposed to 4 different microbiome treatments. The first part of the project will focus on performing exploratory analyses to understand the relationship between host genomic processes and microbiome variations that have a significant impact on the plant fruit chemistry and other phenotypes, with a particular focus on host-microbiome interactions. Subsequently, statistical and machine learning models will be applied to better understand the biological mechanisms and pathways involved, to help design a second trial aimed at testing predictions generated from the data.

  Our research

  As part of the projects, the postdoctoral fellow will collaborate with the wider team, that additionally includes researchers at the Department of Food Science (UCPH), Aarhus University and Aalborg University. The candidate will also have an opportunity to interact with the tomato industry, such as Danish based growers. Thus, teamwork and collaboration will be important skills; however, the candidate will also be given ownership over their own research project and deliverables.

  The fully funded postdoctoral fellowship will be hosted at the Section for Hologenomics/Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics at the GLOBE Institute. As such the candidate will also have the opportunity to collaborate with leaders in the fields of world leading experts in population genetics, statistical genetics, computational biology, clinical microbiology, archaeology, evolutionary genomics, and many other related fields of research. The University of Copenhagen is a world-leading institution of higher learning and provides excellent programs in genetics, archaeology, statistics, computer science and mathematics.

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• PhD degree or equivalent doctorate, with a background in one or more of the following areas: statistics, data science, statistical genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, and/or mathematics

• Experience working in the UNIX operating environment 	
• Excellent English skills written and spoken   Desirable experience and skills:

• Experience with high-performance computing clusters/systems 	
• Experience with compiling and working with data from different sources 	
• Understanding of FAIR data principles, interest in Open Data 	
• Interest in scientific communication and/or public outreach   Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Section for Hologenomics, Oester Farimagsgade 5, 1353 Copenhagen C.

 The Globe Institute is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen. The Institute’s main purpose is to address basic scientific questions through interdisciplinary approaches. The institute operates at the intersection of natural and medical sciences and the humanities. Information on the institute can be found at: http://www.globe.ku.dk/.

  The Globe Institute is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where employees and students can belong and thrive. See website for more information. All qualified applicants will receive full consideration. Candidates who, through their research, teaching, and/or service, contribute to diversity and competencies of our Institute are encouraged to apply. The University of Copenhagen strives to offer a family friendly and flexible working environment with a sustainable balance between work- and private life, including parental leave schemes (up to 47 weeks for both parents) and up to six weeks of paid holidays per year. Researchers that have not been tax liable in Denmark for the last 10 years can apply for a special (reduced) tax scheme. The university offers a variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families.

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The psoition is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is on 1st of April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  Questions

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

jobs.occupation: Metabolite Imaging at Cellular Resolution
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Environmental Science programme. The position is available from 01 February 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title:
Metabolite Imaging at Cellular Resolution

Research area and project description:
This project will develop advanced methods and open-source tools for processing, analysing and interpreting MSI and spatial metabolomics data, particularly for small molecules metabolites at cellular resolution. The methods will be applied to tissue sections, microbial communities, environmental samples to understand spatial control of metabolites and their flux in an organ system.

The successful candidate will work at the interface of computational science, biochemistry, microbiology and analytical chemistry. The project will combine analytical and computational method development with experimental spatial metabolomics workflow combining MALDI-MS, tissue staining and microscopic imaging. The PhD student will join an interdisciplinary team of chemists, microbiologists, biologists and computational scientists and contribute to both methodological development and biological applications.

The position includes:
• Developing mass spectrometry imaging workflows to achieve cellular resolution.
• Integrating various imaging and staining modalities with MSI.
• Collaborating with computational scientists and biologists to validate methods against experimental and biological datasets. Ensure reliable implementation of automated quality control, testing, documentation and reproducibility reporting.
• Communicating computational results clearly to interdisciplinary and non-computational researchers. Processing and analysing imaging datasets and presenting results at internal and international scientific meetings.
• Publishing methodological and application studies and releasing well-documented open-source soft-ware.
• Close supervision and collaboration with dedicated researchers and senior investigators.

We are seeking highly motivated candidates with a strong interest in interdisciplinary research. Applicants should hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in computer science, bioinformatics/ cheminformatics, AI/ML, da-ta science, chemistry, computational biology, chemometrics, analytical chemistry or a related discipline.

• Solid background in analytical chemistry, biotechnology, mass spectrometry, omics data analysis and/or mass spectrometry
